name: LOG
description: LOG returns the logarithm of a number to a specified base. If the base is omitted, it defaults to 10.
tldr: Returns the logarithm of a number to a given base (default 10).

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The positive real number for which you want the logarithm.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: The base of the logarithm. Optional; defaults to 10 if omitted.

basicExample.explanation: With the base omitted, LOG uses 10; 10³ = 1000, so the result is 3.

advancedExamples.title: Logarithm in base 2
advancedExamples.scenario: Measuring bits or orders of magnitude.
advancedExamples.explanation: 2³ = 8, so the base-2 logarithm of 8 is 3.

howItWorks: LOG computes log_base(number), the exponent to which the base must be raised to equal the number. When base is omitted it defaults to 10. Mathematically LOG(n, b) = LN(n) / LN(b).

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: The number must be positive; otherwise #NUM!.
The base must be positive and not equal to 1; base 1 returns an error.
Omitting the base yields base 10, which some users confuse with natural log.

commonErrors.cause: Number is 0/negative, or base is invalid (e.g. 1 or negative).
commonErrors.fix: Use a positive number and a positive base other than 1.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: LOG works identically in Google Sheets, defaulting to base 10 when omitted.

faq.question: What base does LOG use when I omit the base?
faq.answer: Base 10. Use LOG10 for an explicit base-10 log, or LN for base e.

faq.question: How do I compute a natural logarithm?
Why does LOG return #NUM!?
faq.answer: Usually because the number is not positive, or the base is 1 or negative.
